nine template bands. No `code_section`: this page renders no <LocalTrust>, so there is no

migrated cosmetic pages. The block list below is the TEMPLATE's order and the live
toc_links agree with it, so nothing has to be reconciled — but a reviewer coming from the
porcelain-veneers entry will read past it if they are skimming.
THE BAND VALUES ARE READ OFF THIS SHEET AND THEY CONTRADICT THE TEMPLATE'S OWN COMMENTS.
Three section comments in the file said "cream" for `.section.alt` — the WHAT, CANDIDACY
and COST bands. They were wrong. `.singletooth .section.alt` is
background: var(--vs-charcoal-green) at single-tooth-dental-implants.css:231, with h2 #fff

CHARCOAL and two are SAGE-PALE, and none of the five is cream. The comments in the template
have been corrected in the same commit as this entry; each `band_evidence` below names the
rule it was read from, not the class and not the comment.
THIS PAGE'S `cards` REPEATER HOLDS TEN ROWS AND BOTH GROUPS ARE MOVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED.
Confirmed live: five rows in group `whyCards` and five in group `benefitsCards`, each
carrying title, body and a meta of "01"…"05". That is the opposite of porcelain-veneers,
where the repeater came back empty and every card had to be transcribed. The template still
renders its own local arrays (single-tooth-dental-implants.astro:64-120) because it was
written before those rows existed; the strings are identical and the rows are the source of
truth, so the two `card_grid` blocks below move them.
THE COST BAND IS THE PORCELAIN-VENEERS SHAPE WITH ONE DIFFERENCE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE
BAND. It is a standalone <section> holding a .section-head and a one-tier <PricingTiers>
(single-tooth-dental-implants.astro:585-614) — the shape `pricing_tiers` was built for. But
this one is `.section.alt`, so `band` is charcoal where that page's is paper. That is
exactly why `band` is a field on the layout rather than a constant in PricingTiersBlock.
This page also uses the THIRD price slot the veneers page deliberately leaves empty: it
passes priceQualifier 'Starts at' (:597), so `price_note` is filled here and absent there.
THREE GAPS, AND ALL THREE ARE LAYOUT FAULTS RATHER THAN COPY FAULTS. `#compare`'s bullet
lists are not in the comparison_cards selection set; `#benefits` is five across against a
select that stops at four; and both bespoke insets come back as media_split's
`.veneers-callout` aside, losing their `.label` eyebrow. Each is recorded on its own block
with what closes it. None of them is closed by anything in this file.
CTA ROWS SPLIT THE SAME TWO WAYS AS BOTH WORKED EXAMPLES, and the split is the components'
decision, not this file's. `compare` and `process` draw their rows entirely from the
component and their layouts have no cta sub-fields, so nothing is supplied for them; `what`
and `faq` gate their row on cta_label being filled, so those two carry a transcribed pair.
All nine `sections` rows on this page return ctaLabel and ctaHref null — verified live — so
there was never anything to move.

WHAT CLOSES IT is precisely what closed the process one: a '5' => '5' choice in

AND IT NEEDS THE BREAKPOINT LESSON THAT ROUTE LEARNED THE HARD WAY. porcelain-veneers'

adds no specificity, so a scoped `.why-grid.cols-5` at (0,3,0) beats the page sheet's
`.singletooth .benefits-grid` collapses at (0,2,0) and would draw five across INSIDE
this page's own 1240px and 1100px queries (:717, :730). Any cols-5 rule added to
CardGridBlock has to carry its own collapses, as ProcessStepsBlock's now does.
THE CLASS NAMES CHANGE, AND THAT IS SEPARATE. CardGridBlock always emits
`.why-grid` / `.why-card` (CardGridBlock.astro:172) — the component's header says in
as many words that `.why-grid` is the family's name for this grid and not a name about

(single-tooth-dental-implants.css:562-582) stop matching and the block's own card styles
take over. Those are close but not identical: the block's card has 30px 26px 32px padding
and a 36px figure against this page's 30px 24px 28px and 34px, and the block's h3 is 19px
against this page's 18px. Small, uniform across the family, and arguably the point of a
block library — recorded so it is not read as a regression.
The rules are NOT deleted from the sheet. The else branch of the migration switch is the
rollback path and it still renders `.benefits-grid`.
NOTHING IS LOST. All five cards, their headings, their paragraphs and their numbering
come back. This gap is entirely about how many sit in a row and what they are called.
